issues.title: Editorial nits: consistency Receipt section mislabels and typos
issues.author: dcondrey
issues.body:
A few small editorial issues in draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md, offered ahead of adoption review.

In the "COSE Receipt of Consistency" section, the two introductory lines still refer to an inclusion proof: "The cbor representation of an inclusion proof is:" and "The unprotected header for an inclusion proof signature is:". Both appear to be copy-paste from the inclusion section and should read "consistency proof".

The consistency verification steps contain a typo, "From the peaks for tres-size-2", which should be "tree-size-2".

The supporting algorithm is introduced under the heading "consistency_proof_path" but the function it defines is named "consistency_proof_paths" (plural); the heading and the function name could be aligned.

There are two doubled-word typos: "the index of the the right child of i" in add_leaf_hash, and "Returns the mask for the the most significant bit in pos" in most_sig_bit.

issues.title: Security - leaf and interior nodes are not domain separated
issues.author: robinbryce
issues.body:
**Problem**

Interior nodes are computed as `H(pos || left || right)` ([lines 524 to 528](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L524-L528)). Leaves are `H(x)` for whatever bytes `x` the application supplies. Nothing stops an application, or a party that controls leaf content, from choosing `x = BE64(pos) || left || right`. That leaf then hashes to exactly the same value as the interior node at `pos`. No collision search is needed; the preimages are identical bytes.

Because the draft allows an inclusion proof to start at any node ([the index comment in the CDDL](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L127)) and describes verification as applying the proof to "a possible entry (set member) bytes" ([line 240](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L240)), a CDDL-valid proof `{index: 2, path: [v]}` verifies the bytes `X` against the genuine signed peak even though `X` was never appended as a leaf. Anton gives the full four-leaf construction in section 1.3 of his review.

The sentence at [line 103](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L103) saying position binding guarantees uniqueness "without imposing constraints on inputs" overstates what `pos` gives us: it separates interior nodes from each other, not from leaves.

**Raised by**

[Michael Msebenzi, 4 Aug 2026](https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/msg/scitt/Gm7bYrkYM4BLx1LxVTMYQqgmjK0/) (item 3), [Michael Msebenzi, 25 Aug 2026](https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/msg/scitt/HWPYQ8jQmXGF2Jrl-ZOBQARf08w/) (item C), [Henri Sirkkavaara, 28 Aug 2026](https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/msg/scitt/o8f2ZrjOnG6jJ67M54akLAw-ReI/), [Anton Sokolov, 28 Aug 2026](https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/msg/scitt/Jyy9yI2uTtB4RrDaGGi6E1YCUR0/) (section 1.3). All three reviewers rank this first.

**Options**

1. RFC 6962 / RFC 9162 style separation: `H(0x00 || x)` for leaves and `H(0x01 || pos || left || right)` for interiors. See [RFC 9162 section 2.1.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9162.html#section-2.1.1) and [RFC 6962 section 2.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6962.html#section-2.1). Cleanest, but it changes every node value and breaks existing deployments.
2. Keep the hash construction and close the gap procedurally:
   - verifiers of an entry MUST check `index_height(index) == 0`, or the draft separately defines what a proof of an interior node means;
   - `consistent_roots` deduplicates by position, not value (separate issue);
   - a Security Considerations subsection explains that leaf values are application defined, that a party controlling leaf bytes can make a leaf equal an interior node, why the leaf-height check and position binding make this harmless for receipts, and recommends that applications domain separate their own leaf inputs.

Option 2 preserves compatibility and is the suggested direction, but the choice should be put to the working group explicitly since option 1 is what RFC 9162 does.

**Also**

Reword [line 103](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L103) so it does not claim uniqueness across leaves and interior nodes.

---
Raised from the SCITT list reviews of the -03 text (main at 54b1b33). Line links are permalinks to that commit so they stay valid as fixes land.

issues.title: Security - the index is not authenticated when the inclusion path is empty
issues.author: robinbryce
issues.body:
**Problem**

When the inclusion path is non-empty, each step hashes a parent position, so a wrong `index` produces a wrong root and the index is effectively bound to the signature. When the path is empty, which the draft legitimately allows for a node that is itself a peak ([line 230](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L230)), the payload is just the node value. The `index` in the unprotected header can then be rewritten (say from 7 to 0) without changing the payload or the signature result.

`included_root` ([lines 269 to 303](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L269-L303)) returns `nodehash` unchanged in this case, so nothing in verification notices.

**Raised by**

[Anton Sokolov, 28 Aug 2026](https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/msg/scitt/Jyy9yI2uTtB4RrDaGGi6E1YCUR0/) (section 1.5, second part).

**Suggested fix**

Add Security Considerations text stating that the index in the unprotected header is authenticated only through recomputation of the path; in the empty-path case it is not authenticated at all. Applications that need an authenticated position must either bind the position into the leaf content or obtain a proof against a later tree state in which the node is no longer a peak.

---
Raised from the SCITT list reviews of the -03 text (main at 54b1b33). Line links are permalinks to that commit so they stay valid as fixes land.

issues.title: Pseudocode defects - all_ones never returns true so index_height loops forever
issues.author: robinbryce
issues.body:
**Problem**

`all_ones` ([lines 689 to 693](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L689-L693)) reads:

```python
msb = most_sig_bit(pos)
mask = (1 << (msb + 1)) - 1
return pos == mask
```

But `most_sig_bit` ([lines 669 to 671](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L669-L671)) returns a **mask** (a single set bit), not a bit **index**. So for `pos = 1` the mask is 3, for `pos = 7` it is 255, and `all_ones` is never true for any input. `index_height` ([lines 573 to 579](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L573-L579)) then spins at `pos = 1` and never returns. Every core algorithm calls `index_height`, so as written none of them terminate. Three reviewers independently executed the text and hit this.

**Reference implementation**

This is a transcription error in the draft only. [all_ones in algorithms.py](https://github.com/robinbryce/merkle-mountain-range-proofs/blob/8c013b9777ceacb70873172ad142042f01294d41/algorithms.py#L253-L257) uses the bit index:

```python
imsb = pos.bit_length() - 1
mask = (1 << (imsb + 1)) - 1
return pos == mask
```

**Raised by**

[Michael Msebenzi, 4 Aug 2026](https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/msg/scitt/Gm7bYrkYM4BLx1LxVTMYQqgmjK0/) (item 2), [Michael Msebenzi, 25 Aug 2026](https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/msg/scitt/HWPYQ8jQmXGF2Jrl-ZOBQARf08w/), [Henri Sirkkavaara, 28 Aug 2026](https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/msg/scitt/o8f2ZrjOnG6jJ67M54akLAw-ReI/), [Anton Sokolov, 28 Aug 2026](https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/msg/scitt/Jyy9yI2uTtB4RrDaGGi6E1YCUR0/) (section 1.1).

**Suggested fix**

Replace the first line with `imsb = bit_length(pos) - 1` (the draft already defines `bit_length` at [lines 680 to 682](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L680-L682)), or write `mask = (most_sig_bit(pos) << 1) - 1`. With that single change, Anton reports that `index_height`, `peaks`, `inclusion_proof_path` and `included_root` all reproduce correctly across thousands of cases.

---
Raised from the SCITT list reviews of the -03 text (main at 54b1b33). Line links are permalinks to that commit so they stay valid as fixes land.

issues.title: Pseudocode defects - add_leaf_hash relies on an unstated append return convention
issues.author: robinbryce
issues.body:
**Problem**

The draft describes `db` as supporting `append(entry) -> index` ([line 479](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L479)). Readers naturally take that to mean "the index of the entry just appended". Under that reading the loop in `add_leaf_hash` ([lines 489 to 520](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L489-L520)) is one step behind: the condition `index_height(i) > g` and the child offsets `i - (2 << g)` and `i - 1` all point at the wrong nodes, and four leaves produce five nodes instead of seven. Both Henri and Anton reproduced exactly this.

The code is line for line the same as [add_leaf_hash in algorithms.py](https://github.com/robinbryce/merkle-mountain-range-proofs/blob/8c013b9777ceacb70873172ad142042f01294d41/algorithms.py#L5-L30). The difference is that the reference implementation's docstring ([lines 12 to 13](https://github.com/robinbryce/merkle-mountain-range-proofs/blob/8c013b9777ceacb70873172ad142042f01294d41/algorithms.py#L12-L13)) states a convention the draft omits: `append` must return the index for the **next** item, that is, the node count after the append. Under that convention the code is correct. So neither reviewer misread; the text is under-specified.

**Raised by**

[Henri Sirkkavaara, 28 Aug 2026](https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/msg/scitt/o8f2ZrjOnG6jJ67M54akLAw-ReI/), [Anton Sokolov, 28 Aug 2026](https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/msg/scitt/Jyy9yI2uTtB4RrDaGGi6E1YCUR0/) (section 1.1).

**Options**

1. Keep the code and state the convention explicitly at [line 479](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L479): `append` returns the index at which the next entry will be stored, so `i` is the index the parent would take if a merge is due. Also state what `add_leaf_hash` itself returns.
2. Rewrite for the natural convention, where `append` returns the index of the entry just stored:

```python
i = db.append(f)
while index_height(i + 1) > g:
    ileft = i + 1 - (2 << g)
    iright = i
    i = db.append(hash_pospair64(i + 2, db.get(ileft), db.get(iright)))
    g += 1
```

Option 2 is suggested: it uses the same `index_height(i + 1) > g` idiom already used by `inclusion_proof_path` and `included_root`, so the document stops asking the same question two different ways, and the spec no longer depends on an unusual return convention.

---
Raised from the SCITT list reviews of the -03 text (main at 54b1b33). Line links are permalinks to that commit so they stay valid as fixes land.

issues.title: Pseudocode defects - right-peaks rule discards the wrong number of peaks
issues.author: robinbryce
issues.body:
**Problem**

The generation rule at [line 343](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L343) says right-peaks are obtained by taking `peaks(tree-size-2 - 1)` and "discarding length(proofs) from the left". That is wrong whenever two or more old peaks land on the same new peak.

Smallest counterexample, MMR(4) to MMR(8): old peaks are `[2, 3]`, new peaks are `[6, 7]`. Both consistency paths (`[5]` for node 2 and `[4, 2]` for node 3) terminate at new peak 6, so right-peaks must be `[node 7]`. Discarding `len(proofs) = 2` from `[6, 7]` yields an empty list. Anton reports the printed rule fails for 1,272 of the 2,080 state pairs in the first 64 complete MMR sizes.

The verifier side already has it right: step 7 at [line 418](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L418) discards "the number of roots returned by consistent_roots". Only the generator text is wrong.

**Reference implementation**

There is no right-peaks generator in algorithms.py to compare against; this is draft-only text.

**Raised by**

[Anton Sokolov, 28 Aug 2026](https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/msg/scitt/Jyy9yI2uTtB4RrDaGGi6E1YCUR0/) (section 1.2).

**Suggested fix**

Change [line 343](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L343) to discard the number of **distinct destination peaks**, which is the length of the list `consistent_roots` returns. Also say that right-peaks are the node **values** at those indices (a `db.get` step), not the indices themselves.

---
Raised from the SCITT list reviews of the -03 text (main at 54b1b33). Line links are permalinks to that commit so they stay valid as fixes land.

issues.title: Pseudocode defects - consistent_roots deduplicates by value instead of position
issues.author: robinbryce
issues.body:
**Problem**

Two adjacent old peaks can legitimately map to a single new peak, so `consistent_roots` ([lines 446 to 462](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L446-L462)) needs to skip duplicates. It does so by comparing hash values: if the newly computed root equals the previous one, it is dropped. Value equality is the wrong test.

Because leaves are not domain separated (separate issue), a leaf peak can have the same value as an interior peak. Anton's construction: MMR(4) with leaves `a`, `b`, `X` where `X = BE64(3) || a || b`. The valid MMR has distinct peaks at indices 2 and 3 with equal values `[u, u]`. For a same-state proof both paths are empty, the true accumulator is `[u, u]`, and `consistent_roots` returns `[u]`, deleting a real peak.

**Reference implementation**

The same value-based comparison is in [algorithms.py line 183](https://github.com/robinbryce/merkle-mountain-range-proofs/blob/8c013b9777ceacb70873172ad142042f01294d41/algorithms.py#L183) (`if roots and roots[-1] == root`), so the reference implementation needs the same fix.

**Raised by**

[Anton Sokolov, 28 Aug 2026](https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/msg/scitt/Jyy9yI2uTtB4RrDaGGi6E1YCUR0/) (section 1.4).

**Suggested fix**

Have `included_root` also return the index at which the path terminated (the stale `Tuple[bool, int]` annotation in [included_root](https://github.com/robinbryce/merkle-mountain-range-proofs/blob/8c013b9777ceacb70873172ad142042f01294d41/algorithms.py#L94-L140) suggests this was once intended), and skip a root only when its terminal index equals the previous one. This also makes it possible to check that every path ends at a peak of tree-size-2 (separate issue).

---
Raised from the SCITT list reviews of the -03 text (main at 54b1b33). Line links are permalinks to that commit so they stay valid as fixes land.

issues.title: Pseudocode defects - consistency cardinality checks are inconsistent
issues.author: robinbryce
issues.body:
**Problem**

Three different statements about how many things must match, none of them complete:

- the prose MUST at [line 430](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L430) requires `len(peaks(ifrom)) == len(accumulatorfrom)`;
- the comment in the pseudocode at [line 450](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L450) talks about `len(frompeaks) != len(proofs)`;
- the loop body indexes all three arrays.

Neither check is actually implemented in the pseudocode, and the failure behaviour is undefined. Extra proof material is silently ignored; short input produces only an accidental indexing error in whatever language the reader is using.

**Reference implementation**

[consistent_roots in algorithms.py](https://github.com/robinbryce/merkle-mountain-range-proofs/blob/8c013b9777ceacb70873172ad142042f01294d41/algorithms.py#L175-L178) checks both lengths.

**Raised by**

[Michael Msebenzi, 25 Aug 2026](https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/msg/scitt/HWPYQ8jQmXGF2Jrl-ZOBQARf08w/) (item 3), [Anton Sokolov, 28 Aug 2026](https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/msg/scitt/Jyy9yI2uTtB4RrDaGGi6E1YCUR0/) (section 1.6).

**Suggested fix**

Require all three lengths (`peaks(ifrom)`, `accumulatorfrom`, `proofs`) to be equal and state that a mismatch MUST be treated as verification failure. Put the check in the pseudocode as well as the prose.

---
Raised from the SCITT list reviews of the -03 text (main at 54b1b33). Line links are permalinks to that commit so they stay valid as fixes land.

issues.title: Pseudocode defects - completeness check for peaks() is unspecified
issues.author: robinbryce
issues.body:
**Problem**

The `peaks` section ([lines 581 to 607](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L581-L607)) says a caller can confirm the MMR is complete by "testing the height of i+1" but does not say what height, or what to do if the test fails. A verifier given a tree size that is not a complete MMR size has no defined behaviour.

**Reference implementation**

[peaks in algorithms.py](https://github.com/robinbryce/merkle-mountain-range-proofs/blob/8c013b9777ceacb70873172ad142042f01294d41/algorithms.py#L204-L223); see also [complete_mmr](https://github.com/robinbryce/merkle-mountain-range-proofs/blob/8c013b9777ceacb70873172ad142042f01294d41/algorithms.py#L396-L414) for how completeness is computed there.

**Raised by**

[Anton Sokolov, 28 Aug 2026](https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/msg/scitt/Jyy9yI2uTtB4RrDaGGi6E1YCUR0/) (section 2.4).

**Suggested fix**

State that `MMR(i + 1)` is complete if and only if `index_height(i + 1) == 0`, and that verifiers MUST reject a `tree-size-1` or `tree-size-2` that is not a complete MMR size. Anton verified this rule on MMR(1) through MMR(8).

---
Raised from the SCITT list reviews of the -03 text (main at 54b1b33). Line links are permalinks to that commit so they stay valid as fixes land.

issues.title: Pseudocode defects - sibling offset overflows 64 bits at the stated maximum height
issues.author: robinbryce
issues.body:
**Problem**

The conventions say all numbers are unsigned 64-bit and heights go up to 63 ([lines 108 to 109](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L108-L109)). But `inclusion_proof_path` ([line 167](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L167)) and `included_root` ([line 293](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L293)) compute `2 << g`, which for `g = 63` is 2^64 and does not fit. Anton also notes that path generation at maximum height would evaluate 2^64 intermediates.

**Raised by**

[Anton Sokolov, 28 Aug 2026](https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/msg/scitt/Jyy9yI2uTtB4RrDaGGi6E1YCUR0/) (section 2.4).

**Suggested fix**

Add an implementation note: a height-63 node is always a peak in a 64-bit addressed MMR, so implementations must test for termination before computing the sibling offset, use wider arithmetic for that one step, or bound supported heights at 62. Low priority, but it is a correctness statement in a Standards Track document.

---
Raised from the SCITT list reviews of the -03 text (main at 54b1b33). Line links are permalinks to that commit so they stay valid as fixes land.

issues.title: Verification procedure - accumulatorfrom is not carried by the wire format or defined as a trust input
issues.author: robinbryce
issues.body:
**Problem**

Step 1 of consistency verification ([line 413](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L413)) says to initialise `accumulatorfrom` to "the peaks of tree-size-1 in the current proof". The consistency proof CDDL ([lines 316 to 337](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L316-L337)) has no such field. `peaks()` returns indices, not node values, so the verifier cannot compute them either. `consistent_roots` needs the trusted old peak **values** ([line 435](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L435)) and the text never says where they come from.

Henri declined to run the consistency path at all for this reason; Michael and Anton both flag it as the first gap in consistency verification.

**Raised by**

[Michael Msebenzi, 4 Aug 2026](https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/msg/scitt/Gm7bYrkYM4BLx1LxVTMYQqgmjK0/) (item 4), [Michael Msebenzi, 25 Aug 2026](https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/msg/scitt/HWPYQ8jQmXGF2Jrl-ZOBQARf08w/) (item 1), [Henri Sirkkavaara, 28 Aug 2026](https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/msg/scitt/o8f2ZrjOnG6jJ67M54akLAw-ReI/), [Anton Sokolov, 28 Aug 2026](https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/msg/scitt/Jyy9yI2uTtB4RrDaGGi6E1YCUR0/) (section 2.1.1).

**Suggested fix**

Define `accumulatorfrom` as a verifier trust input rather than proof content. For the first proof it is an accumulator for `tree-size-1` that the verifier already trusts, for example the detached payload of a previously verified receipt of consistency, or an accumulator obtained from the ledger over an authenticated channel. For each subsequent proof in a cumulative list it is the consistent accumulator output of the previous iteration.

---

issues.title: Verification procedure - cumulative consistency loop never advances past the first proof
issues.author: robinbryce
issues.body:
**Problem**

The numbered procedure at [lines 406 to 424](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L406-L424) is written as if it iterates over a list of proofs, but:

- steps 1 and 2 only ever read "the current proof" and nothing moves to the next one;
- step 9 has an `if` with no `else`, so the failure branch is undefined;
- nothing says how the accumulator computed in iteration `k` becomes the input to iteration `k + 1`;
- nothing requires `tree-size-1` of proof `j` to equal `tree-size-2` of proof `j - 1`.

**Raised by**

[Michael Msebenzi, 4 Aug 2026](https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/msg/scitt/Gm7bYrkYM4BLx1LxVTMYQqgmjK0/) (item 4), [Michael Msebenzi, 25 Aug 2026](https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/msg/scitt/HWPYQ8jQmXGF2Jrl-ZOBQARf08w/) (item 2), [Anton Sokolov, 28 Aug 2026](https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/msg/scitt/Jyy9yI2uTtB4RrDaGGi6E1YCUR0/) (section 2.1.5).

**Suggested fix**

Rewrite as an explicit loop: for each proof `j`, if `j > 0` require `tree-size-1[j] == tree-size-2[j-1]` and set `accumulatorfrom` to the previous iteration's consistent accumulator; compute the consistent accumulator for this proof; after the last proof, verify the signature over the final consistent accumulator. State that any failed check is a verification failure.

---
Raised from the SCITT list reviews of the -03 text (main at 54b1b33). Line links are permalinks to that commit so they stay valid as fixes land.

issues.title: Verification procedure - encoded right-peaks are never consumed
issues.author: robinbryce
issues.body:
**Problem**

The proof carries `right-peaks` as byte strings ([line 335](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L335)) and the generator text at [line 343](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L343) describes how to produce them. But the verification steps 6 to 8 ([lines 417 to 418](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L417-L418)) never read that field. Instead step 6 invokes `peaks()` again, which yields **indices** and cannot recover node values. The verifier therefore has no way to complete the accumulator from what it has been given.

**Raised by**

[Anton Sokolov, 28 Aug 2026](https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/msg/scitt/Jyy9yI2uTtB4RrDaGGi6E1YCUR0/) (sections 2.1.2 and 2.1.3).

**Suggested fix**

Steps 6 to 8 should read: take `right-peaks` from the proof; require `len(right-peaks) == len(peaks(tree-size-2 - 1)) - len(roots)` where `roots` is what `consistent_roots` returned; the consistent accumulator is `roots` followed by `right-peaks`.

---
Raised from the SCITT list reviews of the -03 text (main at 54b1b33). Line links are permalinks to that commit so they stay valid as fixes land.

issues.title: Verification procedure - consistency paths are not required to end at a peak of tree-size-2
issues.author: robinbryce
issues.body:
**Problem**

Nothing requires each consistency path to terminate at a peak of `tree-size-2`. `consistent_roots` ([lines 446 to 462](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L446-L462)) is not passed `ito`, so it cannot check. The SHOULD at [line 424](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L424) about path lengths is the only gesture in this direction and it is not concrete. A path of the wrong length that happens to land on an interior node would still produce a value that gets compared against the signed payload.

**Reference implementation**

Compare [verify_consistent_roots in algorithms.py](https://github.com/robinbryce/merkle-mountain-range-proofs/blob/8c013b9777ceacb70873172ad142042f01294d41/algorithms.py#L267-L305), which does receive the target accumulator.

**Raised by**

[Anton Sokolov, 28 Aug 2026](https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/msg/scitt/Jyy9yI2uTtB4RrDaGGi6E1YCUR0/) (section 2.1.5).

**Suggested fix**

Pass `ito` (`tree-size-2 - 1`) into `consistent_roots`, have `included_root` return the terminal index (see the deduplication issue), and require that each path's terminal index is a member of `peaks(ito)`. This also gives the SHOULD at [line 424](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L424) a precise meaning.

---
Raised from the SCITT list reviews of the -03 text (main at 54b1b33). Line links are permalinks to that commit so they stay valid as fixes land.

issues.title: Verification procedure - inclusion verification input is ambiguous between entry bytes and node hash
issues.author: robinbryce
issues.body:
**Problem**

The prose says the verifier applies the proof to "a possible entry (set member) bytes" ([line 240](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L240)). The algorithm `included_root` takes `nodehash`, an already computed 32-byte value ([lines 258 to 269](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L258-L269)). Leaf addition says the leaf value is `H(x)` ([lines 476 to 478](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L476-L478)). Passing raw entry bytes and passing `SHA-256(entry)` produce different roots, and the verification text never says which one to do, or what a "candidate entry" means when the encoded index is an interior node.

**Raised by**

[Anton Sokolov, 28 Aug 2026](https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/msg/scitt/Jyy9yI2uTtB4RrDaGGi6E1YCUR0/) (section 2.2).

**Suggested fix**

State normatively how `nodehash` is derived from the candidate: either `H(entry)` as in leaf addition, or "application defined and out of scope for this document", but say which. State that the encoded index MUST refer to a leaf when the candidate is an entry (see the domain separation issue), or define separate semantics for interior node proofs.

---
Raised from the SCITT list reviews of the -03 text (main at 54b1b33). Line links are permalinks to that commit so they stay valid as fixes land.

issues.title: Verification procedure - path-length check against provided tree sizes is unsatisfiable for inclusion proofs
issues.author: robinbryce
issues.body:
**Problem**

[line 249](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L249) says the implementation SHOULD check that proof path lengths are "appropriate for the provided tree sizes". An inclusion proof ([lines 124 to 133](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L124-L133)) carries no tree size, so there is nothing to check against. The identical sentence at [line 424](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L424) is fine, because a consistency proof carries both sizes.

**Raised by**

[Michael Msebenzi, 25 Aug 2026](https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/msg/scitt/HWPYQ8jQmXGF2Jrl-ZOBQARf08w/) (item 4), [Anton Sokolov, 28 Aug 2026](https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/msg/scitt/Jyy9yI2uTtB4RrDaGGi6E1YCUR0/) (section 2.2).

**Suggested fix**

For inclusion, reword to a bound derivable from the index alone, for example `len(path) <= 63 - index_height(index)`, or drop the sentence.

---
Raised from the SCITT list reviews of the -03 text (main at 54b1b33). Line links are permalinks to that commit so they stay valid as fixes land.

issues.title: Wire format - inclusion-path CDDL rejects the empty path the prose requires
issues.author: robinbryce
issues.body:
**Problem**

The CDDL at [line 131](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L131) declares `inclusion-path: [ + bstr ]`, which requires at least one element. But the prose at [line 230](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L230) and the `included_root` text at [line 301](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L301) explicitly support a node that is already a peak, whose path is empty. `inclusion_proof_path(7, 7)` returns `[]` in both the draft and [algorithms.py](https://github.com/robinbryce/merkle-mountain-range-proofs/blob/8c013b9777ceacb70873172ad142042f01294d41/algorithms.py#L33-L92). The inner proof `[0, []]` (CBOR `820080`) is therefore valid under the algorithm and rejected by a strict CDDL validator.

**Raised by**

[Anton Sokolov, 28 Aug 2026](https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/msg/scitt/Jyy9yI2uTtB4RrDaGGi6E1YCUR0/) (section 1.5).

**Suggested fix**

Change to `inclusion-path: [ * bstr ]` (or `[ * hash ]` once a 32-byte `hash` type is defined, see the size constraint issue).

---
Raised from the SCITT list reviews of the -03 text (main at 54b1b33). Line links are permalinks to that commit so they stay valid as fixes land.

issues.title: Wire format - detached payload bytes for a receipt of consistency are undefined
issues.author: robinbryce
issues.body:
**Problem**

[line 310](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L310) says the signature is over "the complete accumulator for tree-size-2". [line 420](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L420) says to verify the signature over the consistent accumulator. The accumulator is a **list** of hashes, but COSE_Sign1 signs exactly one byte string. The draft never chooses an encoding: raw concatenation, deterministic CBOR of the array, a hash of the list, or something else. Each choice produces different Sig_structure bytes, so two conforming implementations cannot interoperate.

For inclusion, [line 242](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L242) says the payload is "this value" (the peak) but does not say explicitly that it is the raw 32 bytes.

**Raised by**

[Anton Sokolov, 28 Aug 2026](https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/msg/scitt/Jyy9yI2uTtB4RrDaGGi6E1YCUR0/) (section 2.1.4).

**Suggested fix**

Specify the detached payload bytes exactly for both receipt types. This must match what existing implementations already sign, so the author needs to make the call. For example: consistency payload is the deterministic CBOR encoding of `[ + bstr .size 32 ]`; inclusion payload is the raw 32-byte peak value.

---
Raised from the SCITT list reviews of the -03 text (main at 54b1b33). Line links are permalinks to that commit so they stay valid as fixes land.

issues.title: Wire format - multiple inclusion proofs under one signature have no defined semantics
issues.author: robinbryce
issues.body:
**Problem**

The unprotected header CDDL at [lines 216 to 228](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L216-L228) allows `inclusion-proofs = [ + inclusion-proof ]`, so several proofs may sit under one signature. Each proof produces one peak. In a multi-peak MMR two valid proofs can end at different peaks, but COSE_Sign1 has one payload. The text does not map proofs to candidate entries, does not require all results to be equal, and does not define a combined payload.

**Raised by**

[Anton Sokolov, 28 Aug 2026](https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/msg/scitt/Jyy9yI2uTtB4RrDaGGi6E1YCUR0/) (section 2.2).

**Suggested fix**

Either require exactly one inclusion proof per receipt, or require that every proof in a receipt resolves to the same peak value, which is then the payload, and say how each proof pairs with its candidate entry.

---
Raised from the SCITT list reviews of the -03 text (main at 54b1b33). Line links are permalinks to that commit so they stay valid as fixes land.

issues.title: Wire format - no 32-byte size constraint or rejection rule on proof nodes and peaks
issues.author: robinbryce
issues.body:
**Problem**

Path elements ([line 131](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L131)), consistency path elements ([line 318](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L318)) and right-peaks ([line 335](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L335)) are all typed as bare `bstr`. For an `MMR_SHA256` profile every one of these must be exactly 32 bytes. Without a constraint, a verifier that concatenates a 31 or 33 byte value into `hash_pospair64` silently computes garbage instead of rejecting.

**Raised by**

[Anton Sokolov, 28 Aug 2026](https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/msg/scitt/Jyy9yI2uTtB4RrDaGGi6E1YCUR0/) (section 2.4).

**Suggested fix**

Define `hash = bstr .size 32` (CDDL `.size` control, [RFC 8610 section 3.8.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8610.html#section-3.8.1)) and use it in all three places. State that verifiers MUST reject any proof element of a different length.

---
Raised from the SCITT list reviews of the -03 text (main at 54b1b33). Line links are permalinks to that commit so they stay valid as fixes land.

issues.title: Wire format - tree-size-1 of zero is CDDL-valid but yields a negative index
issues.author: robinbryce
issues.body:
**Problem**

`tree-size-1: uint` ([line 323](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L323)) admits zero. The verification procedure sets `ifrom = tree-size-1 - 1` ([line 347](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L347), [line 414](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L414)), giving `-1`, which contradicts the rule at [line 108](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L108) that all numbers are unsigned 64-bit. The empty tree case has no defined behaviour.

**Raised by**

[Anton Sokolov, 28 Aug 2026](https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/msg/scitt/Jyy9yI2uTtB4RrDaGGi6E1YCUR0/) (section 2.4).

**Suggested fix**

Require `tree-size-1 >= 1` and both sizes to be complete MMR sizes (see the completeness check issue), or define explicit semantics for consistency from the empty tree. Rejection is simplest.

---
Raised from the SCITT list reviews of the -03 text (main at 54b1b33). Line links are permalinks to that commit so they stay valid as fixes land.

issues.title: IANA and references - paired Proofs registry entries and Change Controller are missing
issues.author: robinbryce
issues.body:
**Problem**

The IANA section ([lines 632 to 651](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L632-L651)) requests only an entry in the COSE Verifiable Data Structure **Algorithms** registry. [RFC 9942 section 8.2.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9942.html#section-8.2.1) says:

> It is not permissible to assign points in the "COSE Verifiable Data Structure Algorithms" registry for which no corresponding entry in the "COSE Verifiable Data Structure Proofs" registry exists.

The existing `-1` (inclusion) and `-2` (consistency) Proofs rows apply to verifiable data structure 1 (RFC 9162) only. The registration templates in [section 8.2.2](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9942.html#section-8.2.2) also require a Change Controller, which the draft omits. As written, IANA cannot action the request.

**Raised by**

[Michael Msebenzi, 25 Aug 2026](https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/msg/scitt/HWPYQ8jQmXGF2Jrl-ZOBQARf08w/) (item A), [Anton Sokolov, 28 Aug 2026](https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/msg/scitt/Jyy9yI2uTtB4RrDaGGi6E1YCUR0/) (section 2.3).

**Suggested fix**

Add two Proofs registry requests:

- Verifiable Data Structure: TBD_1; Name: inclusion proofs; Label: -1; CBOR Type: array (of bstr); Description: ...; Reference: this document; Change Controller: IETF
- Verifiable Data Structure: TBD_1; Name: consistency proofs; Label: -2; CBOR Type: array (of bstr); Description: ...; Reference: this document; Change Controller: IETF

and add "Change Controller: IETF" to the existing Algorithms request.

---
Raised from the SCITT list reviews of the -03 text (main at 54b1b33). Line links are permalinks to that commit so they stay valid as fixes land.

issues.title: IANA and references - normative references cite the superseded I-D and omit RFC 9052 and RFC 9162
issues.author: robinbryce
issues.body:
**Problem**

The normative references ([lines 26 to 30](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L26-L30)) cite `I-D.ietf-cose-merkle-tree-proofs`. That document was published as [RFC 9942](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9942.html) in June 2026, and the -03 build still renders the I-D citation. In addition:

- the draft uses COSE_Sign1 structures throughout but cites only RFC 9053 (algorithms), not [RFC 9052](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9052.html) (structures and process);
- [RFC 9942 section 4.4.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9942.html#section-4.4.1) names RFC 9162 as the model registration, and the domain separation discussion needs [RFC 9162](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9162.html) as a reference, at least informatively.

**Raised by**

[Michael Msebenzi, 4 Aug 2026](https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/msg/scitt/Gm7bYrkYM4BLx1LxVTMYQqgmjK0/) (item 1), [Michael Msebenzi, 25 Aug 2026](https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/msg/scitt/HWPYQ8jQmXGF2Jrl-ZOBQARf08w/) (item 5), [Anton Sokolov, 28 Aug 2026](https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/msg/scitt/Jyy9yI2uTtB4RrDaGGi6E1YCUR0/) (section 2.4).

**Suggested fix**

Replace the I-D reference with `RFC9942: cose-receipts`, add `RFC9052` as normative alongside `RFC9053`, and add `RFC9162` (informative or normative depending on how the domain separation issue is resolved).

---
Raised from the SCITT list reviews of the -03 text (main at 54b1b33). Line links are permalinks to that commit so they stay valid as fixes land.

issues.title: IANA and references - TBD_1 is an undefined name inside the CDDL
issues.author: robinbryce
issues.body:
**Problem**

The CDDL fragments at [line 206](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L206) and [line 379](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L379) contain `&(vds: 395) => TBD_1`. `TBD_1` is prose shorthand from the registration table ([line 117](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L117), [line 641](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L641)), not a defined CDDL rule, so the CDDL does not validate as written.

**Raised by**

[Anton Sokolov, 28 Aug 2026](https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/msg/scitt/Jyy9yI2uTtB4RrDaGGi6E1YCUR0/) (section 2.4).

**Suggested fix**

Either use `=> int` in the CDDL and give the value in prose, or define a rule such as `mmr-sha256 = 3 ; TBD_1, requested assignment` and reference it from both fragments. The RFC Editor will replace the placeholder on publication either way, but the CDDL should validate in the meantime.

---
Raised from the SCITT list reviews of the -03 text (main at 54b1b33). Line links are permalinks to that commit so they stay valid as fixes land.

issues.title: IANA and references - remove the inline hash-agility comment that contradicts the editor's note
issues.author: robinbryce
issues.body:
**Problem**

The `hash_pospair64` pseudocode at [line 550](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L550) contains the comment `# Note: Hash algorithm agility is tbd, this example uses SHA-256`. The IANA section's editor's note at [line 645](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L645) has since settled the approach: one SHA-256 identifier (`MMR_SHA256`) now, additional identifiers registered as separate values later. [line 105](https://github.com/robinbryce/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile/blob/54b1b33a5b0f63ae263067a2111584eec732d3cb/draft-bryce-cose-receipts-mmr-profile.md#L105) already fixes `H` as SHA-256 normatively. The stale comment reads as if the question were still open in the algorithm itself.

**Raised by**

[Michael Msebenzi, 25 Aug 2026](https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/msg/scitt/HWPYQ8jQmXGF2Jrl-ZOBQARf08w/), "on the one issue the minutes record as open".

**Suggested fix**

pulls.title: Add Privacy Considerations: position and ordering disclosure
pulls.author: dcondrey
pulls.body:
The Privacy Considerations section currently points only to the generic considerations in the COSE Receipts framework, which does not describe disclosures specific to this profile's Receipt encoding. This is the first of a set of small, independent additions to that section, offered for consideration ahead of adoption review.

This PR adds the "Disclosure of position and ordering" subsection, together with a one-line framing sentence for the section. An inclusion proof carries the node index, and because nodes are indexed in append order (Conventions and Definitions), the index discloses the proven node's absolute position and therefore its ordering relative to any other entry whose index is known. included_root requires i, so the index cannot be withheld from a verifier. A scoped-distribution SHOULD is included.

reviews.author: robinbryce
reviews.body:
Thank you for this contribution. I don't see the need to say more here than is already said here: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9943.html#name-privacy-considerations which is itself inherited via COSE-Receipts

It is understood that order and position are revealed.

And, specific to the accumulator that is the basis for this draft, anyone with a signed accumulator peak, and possession of a limited range of the VDS content (not the metadata or the pre-image) can self assemble receipts. 

This SHOULD would not accomplish anything

Without further explanation of why this is specifically needed in this profile I'm not minded to include this.

pulls.title: Add Privacy Considerations: ledger size and growth disclosure
pulls.author: dcondrey
pulls.body: This PR adds the "Disclosure of ledger size and growth" subsection. A single inclusion index implies the tree contained at least index + 1 nodes when the proven node was appended, a lower bound on ledger size at that time. The inclusion-path length reveals the height of the committing accumulator peak, tightening that bound. A consistency proof carries tree-size-1 and tree-size-2 in the clear, and because a chain of cumulative consistency proofs can be verified together, such a chain discloses the ledger size at each state, that is, its growth over the covered period.

comments.author: dcondrey
comments.body: Following the discussion on #7: this one is purely descriptive, with no normative SHOULD to be toothless. It concerns fields this profile discloses in the clear, `tree-size-1` and `tree-size-2` in a consistency proof, and the size bound implied by `index` and `inclusion-path` length, which are specific to the accumulator encoding rather than the generic order disclosure already noted in RFC 9943. Offered on that basis; happy to drop it if you consider size disclosure self-evident.

pulls.title: Add Privacy Considerations: linkability of Receipts
pulls.author: dcondrey
pulls.body:
Adds a "Linkability of Receipts" subsection to Privacy Considerations. The `index` is permanent, so Receipts sharing an index are linkable to the same entry; Receipts under a shared perfect subtree expose co-location within `2^g` leaves via shared sibling/peak values, without revealing contents.

Now also folds in the disclosure-about-other-entries point (previously #11, closed): sibling and `right-peaks` values are stable subtree identifiers that let an observer correlate Receipts to overlapping tree regions without learning entry content.

comments.author: dcondrey
comments.body: Following #7: descriptive only, no normative text. The index-permanence linkability and the `2^g` co-location bound under a shared peak are mechanics of this profile's proof encoding, not restated from RFC 9943. It now also folds in the point from #11 (closed) about sibling and `right-peaks` values as stable subtree identifiers.

pulls.title: Add Privacy Considerations: confirmation of entry values
pulls.author: dcondrey
pulls.body: Adds the "Confirmation of entry values" subsection.

comments.author: dcondrey
comments.body: This is the one I think stands apart from #7. The leaf is `H(x)` with no per-leaf salt, so a holder of an inclusion Receipt can confirm a guessed entry by recomputing the root, which for a low-entropy domain discloses the content. Unlike the distribution SHOULD in #7, the mitigation here is one the caller can actually apply, adding entropy or a secret salt before insertion, so the SHOULD accomplishes something. Not covered by the generic considerations in RFC 9943.

pulls.title: Add Privacy Considerations: disclosure about other entries
pulls.author: dcondrey
pulls.body:
Part of a set of small, independent additions expanding the Privacy Considerations section, offered for consideration ahead of adoption review.

This PR adds the "Disclosure about other entries" subsection. The sibling values in an inclusion-path, and the right-peaks of a consistency proof, are digests over interior node positions and their child hashes. They do not reveal the content of the other entries they commit to, but they are stable identifiers for the corresponding subtrees, letting a party that observes multiple Receipts correlate them as relating to overlapping regions of the tree.

Every claim is derived from the draft's own mechanics; no references are added, the authors' prose and algorithms are unchanged, and RFC 2119 usage follows the existing text. Submitted as a Contribution under BCP 78/79; DCO signed-off.

comments.author: dcondrey
comments.body: Folded into #9 to avoid a near-duplicate section; the correlation point now sits alongside the linkability discussion there. Closing this in favour of that.

pulls.title: Sign the tree sizes in the receipt of consistency; shape checks become MUSTs
pulls.author: robinbryce
pulls.body:
The receipt of consistency carried `tree-size-1` / `tree-size-2` only in the unprotected `consistency-proof`, so the signature covered the accumulator but not the size it is the accumulator of. When no origin peak is carried into a new peak of `tree-size-2` (a proof from the empty tree, or one where every origin peak is also a target peak) every path is empty, and the same signature verifies at every larger size that adds peaks of the same heights. The presenter, not the signer, then chooses the size a relying party records.

Changes:

- **COSE Receipt of Consistency**: protected header gains `tree-size-1` (`TBD_2`) and `tree-size-2` (`TBD_3`), both REQUIRED, `uint`; interim private use values `-65932` / `-65933`. The unprotected `consistency-proof` structure is unchanged (RFC 9942 compatibility).
- **Verifying the Receipt of consistency**: rewritten as MUSTs — `tree-size-1` from trusted state, never from the receipt; protected sizes equal the first proof's `tree-size-1` and the last proof's `tree-size-2`; each proof's `tree-size-1` equals the running size; fold by `consistent_roots_for_sizes`; `right-peaks` count fixed by the sizes; the path-length SHOULD is a MUST for consistency proofs. The inclusion-receipt SHOULD is unchanged (no declared size there).
- **`consistent_roots_for_sizes`**: new normative procedure, ported from the reference (robinbryce/merkle-mountain-range-proofs#1). `consistent_roots` is retained as the unconstrained primitive and MUST NOT be used alone. `leaf_count` and `mmr_size_for_leaf_count` added under supporting algorithms.
- **Security Considerations**: new "Declared tree sizes".
- **IANA Considerations**: two COSE Header Parameter registrations (Specification Required range) with the interim values; "no new registries" stands, since these are additions to an existing registry.

Verification: the draft's pseudo-code (with its `-> ERROR` comments turned into raises) was run against `consistent_roots_for_sizes` from the reference repo on all 231 complete size pairs up to 39 and on the negative shapes (non-growing, incomplete target, wrong proof count, wrong path length, differing roots under one target peak); every result agrees. `make` (kramdown-rfc, xml2rfc txt/html) builds clean.

Context: forestrie ADR-0066 (forestrie/devdocs#194), label registry (forestrie/protocol#9), Linear FOR-568. The draft still cites the I-D name for what is now RFC 9942; updating that reference is out of scope here.
